assumptions.statement: The wall reacts the whole weight of the product and its contents.
assumptions.why: Every load path must terminate somewhere, and the only external body in the scenarios is the wall.
assumptions.would_be_invalidated_by: a scenario in which the product also rests on a shelf or the floor

assumptions.statement: The items are discrete and separable from one another.
assumptions.why: Releasing exactly one presupposes that one can be distinguished from the rest; a continuous medium could not be counted.
assumptions.would_be_invalidated_by: a statement that the contents are granular, powdered or liquid

evidence_route_verdict.note: that the two closures are never open together is a mobility claim

obligations_created: a linkage that keeps the two closures out of phase
a volume between them sized to one item
a return to the rest state

derivation_premises: Items that are not contained cannot be dispensed one at a time.
obligations.statement: A volume holds the items before release and admits more from above.

derivation_premises: Releasing one requires separating one from the rest.
Two leaving at once is the same event failing, not a different requirement.
obligations.statement: Exactly one item passes the release boundary for each actuation, and never more than one.

derivation_premises: An actuation the user cannot reach cannot be performed.
obligations.statement: A user-operated surface causes the release and is reachable while the product is fixed in place.

derivation_premises: Refilling in place means the filling path does not pass through the fixing.
obligations.statement: A path exists by which items are added from above while the product remains fixed.

derivation_premises: Whether a group of loose items keeps feeding depends on how they bear on one another, which is a contact question.
obligations.statement: Release continues to occur when few items remain.

derivation_premises: An unreacted load accelerates the body carrying it.
The product is fixed to a wall, so the wall is where its load leaves it.
obligations.statement: The weight of the product and its contents reaches the wall through a connected path.

derivation_premises: A part with no path into the partly built product cannot be installed.
obligations.statement: An ordered installation sequence exists in which every part has a clear path, ending with the product fixed to the wall.

derivation_premises: Capacity is a consequence of the volume and the item size, neither of which is stated yet.
obligations.statement: The number of items the volume holds is about twenty.

unresolved.decision: how one item is separated from the group
unresolved.why_open: Five principle families meter a discrete quantity and the requirements name none. Two of the five depend on contact or deflection, for which no route exists here; three make the claim geometrically. That difference is a fact about the available evidence, not a reason to prefer one.

alternatives: it does not return between uses
unresolved.decision: whether the pressed surface returns on its own or is returned by the user
unresolved.why_open: The requirements say the surface is pressed and do not say what happens after. Every candidate creates a return obligation and none of them is required by the input.

alternatives: a fixing that penetrates the wall
a fixing that bears on the wall surface

unresolved.decision: how the product is fixed to the wall
unresolved.why_open: The wall is the reaction site for every load in the product and nothing about it is stated: not its construction, not the permitted fixings, not the orientation of the mounting face.

unresolved.decision: whether continued release when nearly empty is achievable at all
unresolved.why_open: Whether loose items keep feeding as the group thins is a contact question, and no available evidence route resolves contact. The obligation is recorded and its route is unavailable.
